newsitem.title: KENYA: U.N. groups suspend Mogadishu operations.
newsitem.headline: U.N. groups suspend Mogadishu operations.

text.p: U.N. aid agencies, protesting against the kidnap of a local aid worker last month, on Wednesday suspended relief operations in the Somali capital, officials said.

The suspension of relief activities in Mogadishu came after the Somali Aid Coordination Body (SACB), which groups aid agencies and donors, recommended the closure on Monday. Other aid groups outside the U.N. system said they would also halt operations but gave no details.
Expatriate aid workers flew out of Mogadishu on Wednesday to the Kenyan capital Nairobi following the SACB-backed action.
"It means the closure of normal operations like water and sanitation programmes, vaccination and training workshops at least in the short term," a senior U.N. official told Reuters.
The aid groups are protesting against the kidnap of Somali human rights activist Hilal Aden of the Life and Peace Institute agency (LPI).
The SACB says he is being held without proper medical treatment since being kidnapped in north Mogadishu on September 19.
